claim: In umbrella-sampling simulations of a pair of tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles with brush repulsion and Asakura-Oosawa depletion, at compression ratio 0.6, size ratio 1.21 and depletant-to-lobe radius ratio 0.02, the free energy without depletant rises steadily as the pair approaches -- the rotational-entropy cost of interlocking -- while adding depletant creates a local minimum at the staggered bonding separation (1.229 um), and a depletant volume fraction of 0.05 removes the entropic barrier and makes the staggered bond the global minimum.

numbers.name: depletant_volume_fraction
numbers.note: the depletant volume fraction at which the barrier is gone: parameter of an implicit AO potential; the paper does not say whether it is the reservoir or the system fraction.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles modelled as five spheres (four lobes and one central sphere for the patches) with an Alexander-de Gennes brush repulsion plus Asakura-Oosawa depletion (parameters in the SI, not in the file); Langevin dynamics in HOOMD-blue v2.9.7. Harmonic restraint on the centre separation with spring constant 3,333 kT/um^2, 40 windows with rest lengths from 1.16 to 3 um, 2e8 steps per window with the second half analysed by WHAM. The geometry matches the experiment. The authors contrast this with the DNA patch-patch model of their reference 10, whose landscape follows the purely entropic curve until the patches touch and then has a narrow minimum behind an entropic barrier.
